faq.q: How long does it take for spilt milk to smell in a car?
faq.a: Often a few days. The milk soaks into the underlay, and bacteria break it down while it stays damp, so the sour smell usually shows up on the first warm day with the windows shut.

faq.q: Will bicarbonate of soda get rid of a milk smell in my car?
faq.a: It can soak up some smell from the surface once the area is dry. It won't remove milk that has soaked into the underlay or seat foam, so if the smell comes back, the milk itself needs to come out.

faq.q: Should I use hot water to clean spilt milk?
faq.a: No, use cold water. Hot water can set milk proteins into the fibres. Dab a little on, then blot it straight back out.

faq.q: Will an air freshener cover a sour milk smell?
faq.a: Only for a while. The milk is still in the carpet, and the smell returns once the scent fades or the car warms up.

faq.q: Do I need to be in the car while you do an ozone treatment?
faq.a: No, and you mustn't be. Ozone is only used in an empty car, and the car is aired out before anyone gets back in.

Spilt milk in the car is one of those things that seems fine on the day and smells awful a few days later. The milk runs through the carpet into the foam underlay, stays damp, and goes sour, usually just in time for the first warm afternoon.

The first hour matters most: mats out, blot hard with towels, a little cold water, blot again, then dry it out. Our new guide covers what to do straight away, how to get the smell out yourself, and when it needs proper extraction.
share.instagram:
Spilt milk in the car? Blot it, don't rub it 🥛

Get the mats out, press towels hard into the patch until nothing more comes up, dab on a little cold water (not hot) and blot again. Then stand on a dry towel for a minute to pull milk up from the underlay, and leave the doors open to dry it. If it still smells sour a few days later, the milk is in the underlay and needs extracting, not an air freshener.
